audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers build the entire matchup on "commit when Relentless Pursuit is down" — it is named nine times across the page — and neither layer mentions that Lightslinger attacks REDUCE Relentless Pursuit's cooldown. The page treats the dash as a fixed timer you can count.
audit.why: You cannot count it. Relentless Pursuit is 16s at rank 1, but every Lightslinger double-shot he lands pulls it forward, so a Lucian free-hitting the wave has it back in a fraction of that while a Lucian denied CS genuinely does not. That reverses the causality the page teaches: you do not wait for the dash, you starve it. Denying him the wave IS the dash-tracking plan, and it is the one line of advice that makes "commit when it's down" achievable instead of hopeful.
audit.corrected: The Lightslinger cooldown reduction written in, with the 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s base, and the commit rule re-keyed to denying him attacks rather than counting seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown number appears on the page, though the phrase "on the Relentless Pursuit timer" or equivalent appears in five separate fields.
audit.why: The numbers change the plan rather than decorate it. Relentless Pursuit is 16s base but shrinks with every Lightslinger hit; Piercing Light is 9/8/7/6/5s at only 500 range; Ardent Blaze is 14/13/12/11/10s at 900; The Culling is 110/100/90s at 1400. Piercing Light being 500 range on a 9s cooldown is the specific reason a level-2 step-up is free: he has to be almost in hammer range to use his own poke.
audit.corrected: Relentless Pursuit 16s (reducible), Piercing Light 9s at 500, Ardent Blaze 14s at 900 and The Culling 110s at 1400 written into the spikes, mid and cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says to avoid "feeding one into his Culling resets". The Culling has no reset in Riot's text — it is simply a torrent of shots on a 110/100/90s cooldown at 1400 range. The only cooldown reduction anywhere in his kit is Lightslinger shortening Relentless Pursuit.
audit.why: A reader who believes the ult resets will play around a threat that does not exist and will misjudge how long he is safe after it is spent — which is nearly two minutes at rank 1, and is the single biggest window this lane offers.
audit.corrected: The reset claim removed and replaced with the real 110s window; the actual reset mechanic (Lightslinger into Relentless Pursuit) put where it belongs.

notes: THE INTERACTION THAT WAS MISSING: Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown. Both layers name Relentless Pursuit nine times and hang the whole matchup on "commit when it's down", while treating it as a fixed 16-second timer you can count in your head. You cannot — a Lucian free-hitting the wave refunds it continuously, and a Lucian denied CS does not. That inverts the advice from "wait for the dash" to "starve the dash", which is a thing the reader can actually do. FACTUAL ERROR: content.late warns about "his Culling resets". The Culling has no reset in Riot's text; it is a 110/100/90s projectile at 1400 range. The only cooldown refund in his kit is the Lightslinger one above, and misplacing it costs the reader the biggest window the lane offers — nearly two minutes of a spent ultimate. Cooldowns added: Relentless Pursuit 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s (reducible), Piercing Light 9/8/7/6/5s at 500 range, Ardent Blaze 14/13/12/11/10s at 900, The Culling 110/100/90s at 1400. LEVEL CHART: four stages disagreed with their own whys — Level 1 read Skill above "gate-Q his step-up for free", Level 6 read Skill above "tips to him at 6", first item read Jayce above "Contested item window", and 2+ items read Jayce above "He out-scales". Corrected to Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Lucian/Skill/Lucian. FLAG MISFIRE, deliberately NOT acted on: _missing-interactions.json lists needs-antiheal for this matchup, citing Lightslinger. Riot's text for Lightslinger has no self-healing — it references being healed or shielded BY AN ALLY. The derived heal flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact, so I did not add Grievous Wounds advice to a matchup where nothing heals.
